title: Resilient Error Boundary State Machine with Reset Trigger
problemStatement: Implement `createErrorBoundaryManager({ fallbackRenderer, onError })` that intercepts component exceptions, transitions to an error state with the captured error info, and provides a `reset()` method to restore normal rendering.
interviewTrap: Error boundaries do NOT catch errors in: event handlers, asynchronous code (setTimeout), server-side rendering, or errors thrown in the error boundary itself.

testCases.name: Catches runtime error and activates fallback renderer
testCases.testFn: const eb = createErrorBoundaryManager({ fallbackRenderer: (err) => 'Fallback: ' + err.message }); eb.catchError(new Error('Crash')); return eb.render(() => 'Child');

testCases.name: Reset method clears error state and restores child renderer
testCases.testFn: const eb = createErrorBoundaryManager({ fallbackRenderer: (err, reset) => { reset(); return 'resetting'; } }); eb.catchError(new Error('Crash')); eb.reset(); return eb.render(() => 'ChildHealthy');

testCases.name: Invokes onError callback with diagnostic error
testCases.testFn: let logged = ''; const eb = createErrorBoundaryManager({ onError: e => logged = e.message }); eb.catchError(new Error('LoggedError')); return logged;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: When a component suspends, it throws a Promise up the Fiber tree. React catches the promise, pauses the render phase for that branch, renders the nearest Suspense fallback, and resumes when the promise resolves.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Error Boundary Lifecycle & Recovery Coordination.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Error Boundary Lifecycle & Recovery Coordination maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why must Error Boundaries still be Class Components in React 18/19?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Because React hooks do NOT have an equivalent for the `componentDidCatch` or `getDerivedStateFromError` lifecycle methods. `getDerivedStateFromError` updates state synchronously during the render phase to show fallback UI, while `componentDidCatch` runs during the commit phase to log errors to monitoring services (Sentry).

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What types of errors do Error Boundaries NOT catch?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Error Boundaries do NOT catch: 1) Event handler errors (`onClick`). 2) Asynchronous callbacks (`setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`). 3) Server-Side Rendering errors. 4) Errors thrown within the Error Boundary component itself (rather than its children).
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of Error Boundary limitations.

realWorldUseCases.description: Capturing component stack traces and logging them to APM tools while rendering recovery UI.

howToExplain.opening: Error Boundaries catch JavaScript exceptions anywhere in their child component tree during rendering, lifecycle methods, and constructors, rendering a fallback UI.
keyPoints: getDerivedStateFromError updates state to render fallback.
componentDidCatch logs error info and component stack traces.
Does not catch event handler or async callback errors.
Reset keys (resetErrorBoundary) allow users to retry failed subtrees.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Error boundaries prevent a single JavaScript error in a non-critical widget from crashing the entire web application.
analogies: Firedoors in a submarine: if one compartment floods (crashes), the firedoors seal that room to keep the rest of the submarine afloat.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting Error Boundaries to catch errors inside onClick handlers.
commonMistakes.why: Event handlers do not run during the render phase; errors there must be caught with standard try...catch.

followUpDeepDive.question: How do you trigger an Error Boundary from an async callback?
followUpDeepDive.answer: By setting state with a throwing function: `const [_, setError] = useState(); setError(() => { throw error; });` — this throws during the subsequent render phase, allowing the Error Boundary to catch it.
